text:
andrew: FYI hitting a weird pattern in eu-west2 this morning — a handful of GPU nodes failing health checks during provisioning. noticed large write flush stalls on local-ssd before kubelet marks node NotReady. :frowning:

kevin: can you paste the kubelet + dmesg snippet? timestamps?

andrew: here's the most common stack from dmesg around the failures (truncated):
```
[1738805001.123456] nvme0: write timeout (cmd 0x1f) seq 4821
[1738805001.223456] nvme0: flush pipeline stalled, blk_mq backlog 512
[1738805001.323456] kernel: blk_update_request: I/O error, dev nvme0n1, sector 1234567
[1738805001.423456] kubelet: node-controller marking node NotReady: disk io errors
```

kevin: ugh. that flush/pipeline wording looks like the firmware flush path regressing. did we roll any NVMe firmware or kernel trees last night in eu-west?

sophie: we did a controlled firmware rollout to a subset in eu-west2 around 02:00 UTC for a vendor patch (fix thermal throttling). rollout ID: fw-roll-2026-03-18. but the rollout was opt-in on a handful of pools.

raj: @sophie can you confirm which pools got it? also correlate with provisioning window (we saw a provisioning spike 02:30-03:10).

sophie: checking… pools: gpu-highmem-2, gpu-preemptible-a. about 45 hosts.

ops-bot: [alert] 1738805050 - gpu-provisioner: 12 provisioning failures in eu-west2 within 15m; correlated with block device errors (nvme). Runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/storage-nvme-firmware.md :rotating_light: 

andrew: repro pattern: if a large ephemeral write (image unpack + model copy) happens while the device does a background flush, the pipeline stalls and subsequent small writes time out. provisioning falls back and we end up with evictions.

kevin: temporary mitigation: throttle parallel image pulls on affected pools and add a node-liveness delay to kubelet (increase kubelet --image-gc-high-threshold?).

raj: we should also pin provisioning away from those pools until we confirm fix. can we add a routing policy in the scheduler for 2h?

sophie: yeah, I can patch the allocation filters: add avoidPools: [gpu-highmem-2, gpu-preemptible-a]. rolling policy applied in 2m.

kevin: for triage, collect iostat -x, nvme-cli smart-log, and blk-mq histograms from one host. andrew can you grab from one of the failed hosts?

andrew: grabbing now. output attached (snips):
```
# iostat -x 1 3
Device: rrqm/s wrqm/s r/s w/s rkB/s wkB/s avgrq-sz avgqu-sz await r_await w_await svctm %util
nvme0n1 0.00 1.00 5.00 420.00 1200 54000 124 8.30 12.4 0.3 12.5 0.10 43.5
```

```
# nvme smart-log /dev/nvme0n1
critical_warning: 0
temperature: 53 C
available_spare: 99%
```

sophie: smart looks fine; this seems like a firmware-level flush path stall under high write concurrency. vendor notes on fw-roll-2026-03-18 mention a change to 'fast flush' path. possible regression.

kevin: plan: 1) immediately avoid pools (sophie patch) 2) add provisioning rate-limit to reduce parallel image pulls (kevin) 3) rollback firmware on 1 host as canary (raj + sophie) 4) if rollback fixes, schedule broad rollback and vendor escalation.

raj: i'll coordinate rollback with vendor. need serial console access and maintenance window for the canary. pref window in 30-60m.

andrew: also, sending a short prompt to infra-cost: this will increase cross-region provisioning and SRE ops for ~2-4h — might spike costs.

kevin: (temporary) command to limit parallel pulls on node: add docker/podman daemon config or set kubelet flag --image-pull-progress-deadline and a mutating webhook to throttle initContainers. I'll draft quick patch. :wrench:

sophie: patch applied: allocation filters live. ops-bot: please mute provisioning alerts for those pools for 10m while we confirm.

ops-bot: [action] muted alert gpu-provisioner/eu-west2 for pools [gpu-highmem-2,gpu-preemptible-a] for 10m.

andrew: can we add an automatic fallback in the scheduler so new requests go to eu-central if eu-west2 capacity is hit? that's what caused the burst hitting the risky pools.

raj: we already have region-fallback policy but it prefers local first; i'll flip it to prefer healthy region for 2h.

kevin: after canary rollback, collect a full nvme trace (blk_trace) and file with vendor. include kernel version, nvme-cli version, dmesg.

andrew: thanks team. i'll monitor provisioning and post followups. tagging @oncall for visibility. :eyes:
